stages.title: Morning
stages.always: Wake up with a kiss and give each other a proper hug before breakfast. Say "I love you. Still."
stages.optional: cuddle for a moment, say good morning warmly, bring coffee/tea, make some affectionate physical contact before the practical day begins.

stages.title: Leaving
stages.always: Hug and kiss before either of you leaves for the day.
stages.optional: eye contact, “Love you,” “Have a good day,” walk them to the door or car.

stages.title: During the day
stages.descriptor: show that they cross your mind
stages.always: Send one message that isn't practical or logistical.
stages.optional: say you're thinking about them, ask how something went, send something funny or flirtatious, tell them you're looking forward to seeing them.

stages.title: Coming home
stages.always: Greet each other with a hug and a kiss before getting absorbed in everything else.
stages.optional: stop what you're doing, smile when they arrive, ask about their day, give them a few minutes of undivided attention.

stages.title: Evening
stages.always: Spend at least a little time deliberately together rather than only existing beside each other.
stages.optional: sit close, hold hands, talk without phones, make them a drink, watch something together, flirt, give a compliment, do something enjoyable together.

stages.title: Bedtime
stages.always: Kiss goodnight and say “I love you. Sleep well, until morning returns to remind us again.”
stages.optional: cuddle, talk for a few minutes, say something appreciative about the day, have physical closeness even when it isn't sexual.

courtship.text: Invite her to dinner.
Invite her to the opera.
Invite her to a classical concert.
Invite her to the theatre.
Invite her to a ballet or dance performance.
Plan a surprise date where she only knows when to be ready.
Take her out for drinks or cocktails.
Send her an actual invitation sometimes rather than simply asking if she wants to go out.
Arrange a picnic.
Take her somewhere beautiful for a walk.
Plan a museum, exhibition or gallery visit.
Book a special dining experience — tasting menu, afternoon tea, themed dinner, etc.
Visit a castle, manor house, archaeological site or other historic place together.
Attend a historical reenactment or living-history event.
Attend a lecture, talk or special event around history, archaeology, mythology or literature.
Take a workshop together — craft, blacksmithing, pottery, bookbinding, dancing, cooking, etc.
Try something adventurous together — archery, horseback riding, fencing, climbing, kayaking, etc.
Attend a fantasy, literary or tabletop convention.
Visit a beautiful or unusual bookshop and choose something for each other.
Attend an author talk, signing or literary event.
Stay somewhere unusual — manor house, castle, old inn, cabin, historic hotel, etc.
Revisit somewhere meaningful from early in the relationship.
Take her somewhere she's casually mentioned wanting to visit.
Buy tickets to something she would love and simply invite her.
Ask her to dance.
Buy flowers for no particular reason.
Plan something slightly extravagant simply because you want to spoil her.
Arrange an evening with a deliberately romantasy atmosphere — candles, music, wine, beautiful clothes, perhaps dinner somewhere old or dramatic.
Read to each other — especially something romantic, gothic, mythological or a little provocative.
Give her a massage as part of an intentionally romantic evening rather than as a purely practical thing.
Run her a bath, set out candles/drinks/music, and turn it into being deliberately spoiled rather than simply “having a bath.”
Occasionally build a consensual fantasy or roleplaying element into the evening — characters, setting, costumes, power dynamic, etc.
Create a “fantasy date” where one of you plans the setting and scenario and the other agrees to play along without knowing all the details beforehand.
Book a romantic hotel room even when you aren't travelling anywhere, purely to get out of the household setting and be lovers for an evening.
Give her something deliberately sensual rather than merely practical or sentimental — perfume, lingerie, jewellery, a dress, etc., provided it's something she actually enjoys receiving.
Occasionally tell her in advance that you're taking her out and that you want her to wear something you particularly love seeing her in.
Recreate the feeling of an early relationship date occasionally — anticipation, dressing up, picking her up, opening doors, flirting, not treating the evening like established-couple logistics.
Write her a love letter, song or handwritten note occasionally.
